mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4% for three consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE > 4% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for two consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by more than 1% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both FEDFUNDS and RSAFS (real savings) by more than 0.5% in the same month signals a loosening of monetary and savings conditions, which increases liquidity and boosts risk appetite, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during months when both FEDFUNDS and RSAFS decline by more than 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both GDPC1 and HOUST (housing starts) by more than 2% month-over-month indicates a broad-based acceleration in demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both rise > 2% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive when both GDPC1 and HOUST rise by more than 2% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in PAYEMS by more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which increases consumer spending and corporate hiring, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in any macro regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during periods when PAYEMS increases by more than 0.5% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL (core inflation) exceeds 4% while FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for three consecutive months, it signals a lagged policy response to inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 4% and FEDFUNDS < 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL > 4% and FEDFUNDS < 2% for three consecutive months.
